concept.name: Roll yield
concept.definition: The return generated when a futures position is rolled from a near-term expiring contract into a longer-dated contract, arising from the price difference between the two contracts as the near contract converges toward spot. It is positive for long positions in backwardation and negative in contango.
concept.intuition: Because a futures price must meet the spot price at expiry, holding and renewing a position earns (or costs) the gap between the expiring contract and the next one, even if the spot price never moves.
concept.mechanics: To stay exposed without taking delivery, a holder sells the expiring contract and buys the next month. In backwardation the expiring contract is sold at a higher price than the deferred contract bought, generating a positive roll yield; in contango the holder sells low and buys high, generating a negative roll yield. Roll yield plus spot-price change approximates the total return of a futures position.
concept.formula: Roll yield = (total change in futures prices) - (total change in spot price); equivalently for a single roll, approximately (F_near - F_deferred) / F_near for a long position.
concept.failure_modes: Roll yield is realized only if the curve shape persists through the roll window; a curve that flips between rolls turns an expected gain into a loss. It is also path-dependent: rolling on days of anomalous spread widening (e.g. ETF roll windows exploited by other traders) worsens realized roll relative to the quoted curve slope.
concept.misconceptions: Roll yield is not a guaranteed 'carry' return like bond coupon income; it is a consequence of curve shape that can change sign at any time. Commodity-index returns are not spot returns — long-run divergences between the two are largely roll yield, not management error.
concept.example: An investor long 100 crude contracts rolls each month while the market is backwardated by $1 per month: each roll re-establishes the position $1 per barrel cheaper, adding roughly that amount per month to returns even if spot prices are flat.
